hints.title: Streaming Reservoir Node Selection
hints.text: Choosing a node uniformly at random from a singly linked list without prior knowledge of its length can be solved in a single sequential pass.

hints.title: Probabilistic Replacement Over Stream
hints.text: As you inspect the k-th node in the list, replace the currently selected node with probability 1 / k. Mathematical induction proves each node has exactly 1 / n probability.

hints.title: Reservoir Sampling Blueprint
hints.text: Set chosen = head.val, scope = 1, curr = head.next. While curr is not None: generate random float between 0 and 1; if less than 1 / (scope + 1), update chosen = curr.val. Increment scope and curr = curr.next. Return chosen.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in linked list
complexity.notes: Reservoir sampling uses constant auxiliary space without copying list elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Storing all values in an array uses O(N) memory, which fails when the stream exceeds local capacity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant extra memory achieves uniform random selection at the cost of O(N) traversal per pick.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding reservoir sampling proof where probability at node k is 1/k * (k/(k+1)) * ... = 1/n.

solutions.approach: Java Reservoir Sampling with O(1) Extra Space
